answer: A farm emitting 89 variations of one paragraph thus pays for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the canyon panel. Because the entropy is measured at the quill gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the sable audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 6 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. That is 21 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
